\title{The Wrong Unit of Uncertainty:\\
Adaptive Design-Aware Conformal Inference for\\
Repeated Cross-National Surveys}
\author{The Authors}
\date{}

\begin{document}
\maketitle

\begin{abstract}
Comparative research routinely reads a single wave-pair mean contrast and narrates it
as a persistent, distribution-wide, country-level trend---attaching uncertainty to the
wrong unit and over-detecting change. We give a principled instrument: a finite-sample
simultaneous band over a country's whole attitude \emph{trajectory}, with the country as
the exchangeable unit, and a hierarchy of claims (pairwise $\to$ any-pair $\to$ net $\to$
persistent country-wide) whose top rung is the honest object. A second error compounds
it---the calibration objects, other countries' distributions, are not observed but
estimated from complex samples---and we prove this is a hard limit: bands calibrated on
noisily-estimated objects face a non-identification barrier
(Theorem~\ref{thm:impossible}) and a distribution-free reliability floor requiring
$K\ge94$ exchangeable populations (Proposition~\ref{prop:unreach}). Across the two
largest cross-national surveys these barriers bind in opposite ways and never jointly
release, so a design-aware correction is provably unreachable at survey scale. What
remains is the honest procedure for the regime that occurs: a clustered band exact at any
$K$ (Theorem~\ref{thm:exact}) inside a selector that abstains when deconvolution is
unreliable, provably correctly. The payoff is two corrections. In the ESS (2018--2022),
persistent distribution-wide trust decline is certified in one of roughly thirty
democracies (Greece), not the twenty flagged marginally; on the World Values Survey
(1981--2022) the marginal case for Foa--Mounk ``deconsolidation'' over-counts the
persistent phenomenon by $2.6$--$6.5\times$.
\end{abstract}

\section{Proofs and efficiency results}\label{app:proofs}
Full statements and proofs of Theorems~\ref{thm:impossible}--\ref{thm:safe}, the
efficiency results AW-1--AW-3, the open excess-width oracle inequality, and the
modulation self-inclusion deficit are collected in the supplementary theory notes
(\texttt{docs/THEORY\_MAIN.md}, \texttt{docs/DESIGN\_AWARE\_THEOREM.md},
\texttt{docs/ADAPTIVE\_WIDTH\_THEORY.md}). Each theorem has a machine-checked contract
test (\texttt{tests/test\_theorem0.py}, \texttt{test\_deconv\_safe.py},
\texttt{test\_safe\_selector.py}).

\section{Frozen selector specification and validation protocol}\label{app:spec}
The frozen constants ($\rho_0=0.47$, $\delta_{\max}=0.02$,
$\widehat\delta_{\text{UCB}}(D)=0.0061+0.0943\,D$, $g_{\min}=0.10$, margin
$\Delta_g=0.05$, stability floor) and their derivation on the development grid are in
\texttt{docs/SAFE\_SELECTOR\_SPEC.md}. The sealed independent-validation
preregistration, grid, and seed manifest are in
\texttt{docs/INDEPENDENT\_VALIDATION\_PREREG.md} and \texttt{configs/}; results in
\texttt{docs/HOLDOUT\_VALIDATION\_RESULTS.md}.
